title: Operational Coherence
definition: A strategy is operationally coherent when every promised outcome has an owner, an ordered sequence, authorized tools, evidence of completion and a defined escalation path. Activity without these links is motion, not execution.
diagnostic_method: Define evidence and escalation for every critical task
observable_indicators: Every task has one accountable owner
Sensitive actions have an approval gate
decision_rules: Do not activate tasks with unresolved dependencies
Do not mark sensitive work complete without the required approval
Do not delegate to an unvalidated agent

good_examples.situation: A campaign moves from financial review to strategy to operations with evidence at each handoff
good_examples.result: The team can locate responsibility and blockage immediately

bad_examples.situation: Several agents receive the same vague instruction without ownership
bad_examples.result: Work is duplicated and no one can verify completion

limits_and_counterexamples: Creative exploration may begin with looser ownership
Emergency handling may compress sequence but must preserve retrospective evidence
expected_result: Plans become observable execution systems with clear ownership, proof and safe escalation.

relationships.justification: Operational coherence requires persistent evidence and decisions across handoffs.

forbidden_uses: Treating the candidate as approved canon
Using it as evidence of a real-world fact without an external source

review_note: Aprobado por el fundador para el canon piloto Entity Bible v2.
